local_facts.title: A buildout-era housing base
local_facts.claim: Frisco's 2023 comprehensive-plan appendix reports 58,574 single-family housing units; 39.6% were built in 2000–2009, 31.2% in 2010–2019, and 11.4% in 2020 or later.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Many doors may still have the original builder-installed springs, rollers, bearings, and opener parts, so the inspection should look beyond the one component that first caught the homeowner's attention.

local_facts.title: A city permit path and many HOAs
local_facts.claim: Frisco lists replacement doors among its residential self-service permit categories, and the City says Frisco has more than 200 HOAs.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A mechanical repair can often preserve the existing exterior; when a panel or full door must change, the homeowner can verify the city permit path and the applicable association review before finalizing a visible replacement.

local_facts.title: A documented Frisco hail event
local_facts.claim: During the National Weather Service's April 3, 2014 North Texas severe-weather outbreak, trained spotters reported hail up to two inches in Frisco.
local_facts.why_it_matters: After hail or a wind event, a technician should check more than the face of the door: sections, hinges, track alignment, photo-eye brackets, and the door's full travel can all be affected.

anchors.label: Windows and doors replacement permit
anchors.detail: Frisco's consolidated fee schedule prices a window or door replacement permit at $75, then adds $25 for each additional element up to a $150 ceiling. A replacement door is the element being counted.

anchors.label: Inspection outside normal business hours
anchors.detail: What the city charges when an inspection has to happen off the standard weekday schedule. It is the published price of convenience on a permitted job, and it is separate from the permit itself.

anchors.label: Median wage, general maintenance and repair workers
